name: A journal club reading log
scenario: One reader budgets by page count. Figure-led empirical reads tend to finish early; deriving equations by hand often runs long. A short verification of a familiar theorem is a deliberate counterexample.

tasks.title: Reproduce the noise bound
tasks.description: Read the brief proof and derive the missing expectation step on paper before journal club.
tasks.details: The handout is only six pages. The conditioning argument is new.

sections.heading: Setting
sections.body: Two sensors return a count and an independent error with mean zero. The proposed estimator averages repeated readings after a thresholding step.

sections.heading: Reading target
sections.body: Write the conditional expectation of the retained observations. Identify where thresholding breaks the usual zero-mean argument. Derive one corrected expression for a threshold of zero.

sections.heading: Notebook entry
sections.body: Record your assumptions next to the equation they justify and give a small distribution for which the uncorrected claim fails.

tasks.title: Read the cache study for discussion
tasks.description: Skim methods, identify the baseline in Figure 3 and note how the hit rate changes across the three traffic mixes.
tasks.details: Only need talking points, no derivations.

tasks.title: Derive the queue drift inequality
tasks.description: Work through the proof of the drift bound and write the algebra the author skips between lines two and three.
tasks.details: This argument is unfamiliar although I have seen the theorem statement.

tasks.title: Review the storage benchmark
tasks.description: Read the workload definitions and four plots; bring two limitations of the throughput comparison.
tasks.details: I know the workload generator from another class.

tasks.title: Verify one step using Jensen
tasks.description: Check the direction of one inequality in my old notes and record the convexity assumption.
tasks.details: I used this exact proof last semester; not reading the surrounding paper.

tasks.title: Prepare journal club questions
tasks.description: Read the methods and evaluation of the rack placement paper, then make three questions backed by a figure.
tasks.details: Need one careful pass through the results. Skip the analytic appendix.

tasks.title: Reconstruct the mixture proof
tasks.description: Starting with the definition of the mixture, derive both cases in the likelihood proof. Finish with one numerical check.
tasks.details: Looks similar to the noise note but the notation is different.

tasks.title: Skim the results on burst traffic
tasks.description: Understand the run conditions and the tails of the latency plot. Add a slide with one chart and a two-sentence takeaway.
tasks.details: The chart is provided and the deck is open.

holdouts.title: Prepare the calibration reading
holdouts.description: Work through the assigned portion of the short calibration paper and write notes detailed enough to explain the steps at the board.
holdouts.details: My group assigned me the appendix exercise in the reading guide.

pdf.title: Reading guide: calibration under selective labels

sections.heading: Paper outline
sections.body: The main text compares three calibration plots on held-out reviews. The appendix studies a toy censoring rule that hides labels below a decision threshold.

sections.heading: Main-text exercise
sections.body: Choose the most distorted reliability diagram and describe the subgroup responsible. One paragraph is sufficient.

sections.heading: Appendix exercise
sections.body: Derive the calibration error conditional on a label being visible, for both values of a binary grouping variable. Use the censoring rule to construct a counterexample and show the arithmetic.

sections.heading: Discussion
sections.body: Be ready to justify each conditioning step without looking at the printed argument.

holdouts.check: The PDF distinguishes a derivation from the easier main-text exercise.

holdouts.title: Prepare a transport paper for club
holdouts.description: Read the evaluation and give two observations tied to the latency and loss plots.
holdouts.details: Skip the formal congestion-control argument; I only cover the measurement section.
holdouts.check: A broad reading-category correction mixes tasks with opposite errors. The matched empirical reads are more useful.
